title: GDP: Measurement and Limitations
text: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is measured using three approaches: the expenditure approach (summing consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports), the income approach (summing all factor incomes including wages and profits), and the production approach (summing value added at each stage of production). Nominal GDP is measured at current prices; real GDP adjusts for inflation using a price deflator. GDP growth rate is the primary indicator of economic health. However, GDP has significant limitations: it does not capture income distribution, environmental degradation, unpaid work, or the informal economy. Alternative measures include the Human Development Index (HDI), which incorporates health and education alongside income.
